lines.trans: A very good evening to you watching us.
We are starting the presidential debate.
I have here to my left the candidate.
And to my right the other candidate.
To begin, you have one minute to ask a question, please.
Candidate, during your administration the state had the worst unemployment rate.
Do you acknowledge that your economic policy failed?
Your time is running.
I do not know if you understood the question from the candidate.
I heard it.

meanings.note: Agrees with its noun as a determiner/adjective; singular muita coisa idiomatically means many things.

examples.trans: They say a lot of things.

meanings.note: Everyday adjective in tá bom (okay), boa tarde (good afternoon), and Bom, pessoal (Well, folks).
Used in boa noite for both good evening on arrival and good night on departure.

examples.trans: A very good evening to everyone.

meanings.note: Links verbs like faltar to an event or destination.

A person being addressed, with third-person verb agreement: você vai, vocês vão. Vai and vão are forms of ir, not forms of the pronoun. Common in Brazil; not a rule that every Brazilian region uses the same address system.

examples.trans: Are you going to the meeting?

meanings.note: All-purpose connector, relative link, question opener, and comparative word after mais or melhor.

examples.text: Eu acho que ele já foi.
examples.trans: I think that he already left.

meanings.note: First-person plural object pronoun.

examples.text: Boa noite a você que nos acompanha.
examples.trans: Good evening to you watching us.

meanings.note: In broadcasts, a você que nos acompanha greets viewers tuning in.

examples.text: Boa noite a você que nos acompanha.
examples.trans: Good evening to you watching us.

meanings.note: Used here for being present at an event. Vou estar keeps estar in the infinitive after the finite form vou.

examples.trans: I’m not going to be at that meeting.
Are you going to be at that meeting?

meanings.note: Takes a before an infinitive: começa a fazer (starts doing).

examples.text: A gente começa a fazer a pele.

meanings.note: Definite article agreeing in gender and number with its noun; also common before given names in casual Brazilian speech.

examples.trans: Look at the young woman over there.

meanings.note: Formal or televised discussion between candidates or speakers.
Links a meeting with its subject. Do is de + the masculine article o; sou do financeiro identifies membership in the finance department.
Journalistic noun or adjective for a candidate running for president.

examples.trans: The debate of the presidential contenders has begun.
The presidential contenders answered the questions.

meanings.note: Subject form referring to the speaker. Explicit eu introduces his department in the explanation.
Expresses possession, obligation in ter que + infinitive, and impersonal existence (tem alguns números, there are some numbers).

examples.text: Eu tenho que entrar lá dentro.
examples.trans: I have to go inside there.

meanings.note: Points to the speaker's location or reinforces demonstratives like isso aqui and esse slide aqui.

examples.text: Ela veio aqui olhar um extintor.
examples.trans: She came here to check an extinguisher.

meanings.note: First-person singular possessive agreeing with the thing possessed.

examples.text: O seu tempo vale mais que o meu?
examples.trans: Is your time worth more than mine?

meanings.note: Physical side or direction, as in ao meu lado esquerdo (to my left side).

examples.text: Ele está ao meu lado esquerdo.
examples.trans: He is at my left side.

meanings.note: Placed after the noun in Portuguese: lado esquerdo (left side).

examples.text: Tenho ao meu lado esquerdo o candidato.
examples.trans: I have to my left the candidate.

meanings.note: Used both as a noun and as a formal vocative title in political debates.

examples.text: Eu passo a palavra ao candidato.
examples.trans: I give the floor to the candidate.

examples.text: Candidato, o senhor tem um minuto.

meanings.note: Coordinating conjunction pronounced [i] in natural Brazilian speech.

examples.text: Ela faltou e adiantou o trabalho.
examples.trans: She missed it and got ahead on her work.
There are good and bad numbers.

meanings.note: Used after verbs to mean 'properly, right'.

examples.text: A gente não conseguiu encaixar direito.
examples.trans: We could not manage to fit it in right.

meanings.note: Stands without um for another (outro gráfico), or with os for the others (os outros).
Full form of informal pra; introduces purpose before an infinitive or direction.

examples.trans: I have a lot to sort out.

meanings.note: Polite title; saying sim, senhor to an equal coworker adds mock military obedience.

examples.trans: Are you going in now, sir?

meanings.note: Indefinite article; plural uns and umas mean some or a few in everyday Brazilian Portuguese.

examples.trans: Shall we have a little coffee?

meanings.note: Unit of time; um minuto is standard debate timing.
Irregular past eu fiz (I made/did); não tem o que fazer means having nothing to do.

examples.text: Ela não tem o que fazer agora.
examples.trans: She has nothing to do now.

examples.text: Esse slide aqui eu fiz ontem.
examples.trans: This slide here I made yesterday.

meanings.note: In Portuguese, one 'makes' a question: fazer uma pergunta.

examples.text: O senhor pode fazer uma pergunta.

meanings.note: Expresses duration (por uma hora) and fixed phrases like por exemplo.

examples.trans: I stayed there for an hour.

meanings.note: In por favor, the standard polite 'please'.

examples.text: Ei, por favor, não desliga, não!
examples.trans: Hey, please do not hang up!
Can you do me a favor?

meanings.note: Indicates duration across a period of time.
Possessive determiner agreeing with the possessed noun; in Brazil it most often means your (with você).

examples.text: É isso que você quer pra sua vida?
examples.trans: Is that what you want for your life?

meanings.note: Refers to a political administration or term in office.

examples.text: Durante o seu governo, o índice subiu.
examples.trans: During your administration, the rate rose.

meanings.note: A state of the federation or a general condition.

examples.text: O estado teve um índice alto.
examples.trans: The state had a high rate.

meanings.note: Irregular comparative and superlative of ruim (bad).

examples.text: O estado teve o pior índice de desemprego.
examples.trans: The state had the worst unemployment rate.

meanings.note: Statistical rate or indicator, such as índice de desemprego.

examples.text: Esse foi o pior índice do ano.
examples.trans: That was the worst rate of the year.

meanings.note: Lack of formal employment across the economy.
To admit a fact or recognize someone.
Means both politics in general and a specific public policy (política econômica).
Agrees with the noun it modifies: política econômica.
Used for plans, policies, or negotiations that fail.
Refers to someone's time or duration (esse tempo inteiro).

examples.text: Seu tempo vale mais que o meu?
examples.trans: Is your time worth more than mine?
I stayed there that whole time.

meanings.note: With tempo, estar correndo means the clock is ticking.

examples.text: O tempo do senhor está correndo.

meanings.note: A negative answer or a negation in a sentence. A final repeated não can reinforce a conversational refusal in Brazil.
Covers knowing facts or finding out information.

examples.text: Eu só quero saber o motivo.
examples.trans: I just want to know the reason.

meanings.note: Introduces a condition; triggers future subjunctive when referring to a possible future action (se vocês olharem).

examples.text: Se eu vou entrar, você vai também.
examples.trans: If I'm going in, you're going too.

examples.text: Se vocês olharem bem, tem números.
examples.trans: If you look closely, there are numbers.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb for grasping meaning or an explanation.

examples.trans: I don't understand any of this.

meanings.note: Irregular first-person present eu ouço; past eu ouvi.
Time between midday and evening; boa tarde! greets or bids farewell in the afternoon.

examples.text: A reunião é hoje à tarde.
